a11y: Skip link to main content precedes the header.

PrimaryCTA.role: button or link (by effect: navigation=a, action=button)
PrimaryCTA.purpose: The one primary action for the view.

FeatureList.purpose: Specific capabilities stated as user outcomes.

EvidenceBlock.purpose: Sourced proof only (quotes, logos, figures carry a source).

AppShell.purpose: Stable frame for the primary task.
a11y: One main landmark; landmarks are labeled.

TaskList.role: list or grid with row actions
TaskList.purpose: Scan and pick the item to work on.

TaskDetail.purpose: Inspect and act on one item.

StatusToast.purpose: Confirm async outcomes without stealing focus.

MetricTile.purpose: One metric with its truth label (measured/estimated/not measured).

ChartPanel.role: figure with an equivalent data table
ChartPanel.purpose: Show a trend; the table is the accessible equivalent.

DataTable.role: table with caption and scoped headers

MessageList.purpose: Conversation history; new messages announced once complete.

AITrustEnvelope.purpose: One truthful provenance scope per AI response.

SourcePanel.purpose: Sources and context behind an AI answer, when available.

ProgressStepper.purpose: Where the user is in a multi-step flow.

ConfirmationPanel.purpose: Outcome of the flow with next step.

DEFAULT: reachable in tab order if interactive

why it is empty + first action

ERROR: what failed, why, what to do

territories.name: Quiet Precision
territories.thesis: Restrained neutrals, exact alignment, one accent reserved for the primary action.

territories.name: Editorial Warmth
territories.thesis: Content-led pages with generous type scale and sourced imagery doing the persuading.

territories.name: Operational Clarity
territories.thesis: Dense, scannable, status-first layouts for people who work in the tool all day.

steps.system_response: States the offer in one sentence
steps.failure_path: Unclear offer -> visitor leaves; test headline comprehension

steps.system_response: Navigates to the next step or confirms
steps.failure_path: Target unavailable -> explain and offer an alternative contact path

flows.name: Complete the task
flows.goal: User finds an item and updates it

steps.system_response: Shows its detail without losing list position
steps.failure_path: Item deleted elsewhere -> STALE notice with refresh

steps.system_response: Validates, saves, confirms via status toast
steps.failure_path: Save fails -> ERROR with retry; edits preserved

flows.name: Find what needs attention
flows.goal: Operator identifies and opens the item that needs action

steps.system_response: Shows each metric with its truth label and freshness
steps.failure_path: Data unavailable -> UNAVAILABLE state with reason, never a zero

steps.system_response: Updates metrics/table and announces the result count
steps.failure_path: No results -> EMPTY state with clear-filters action

flows.success_signal: Operator reaches the item needing action

screens.purpose: Get a trustworthy answer or draft

flows.name: Ask and verify
flows.goal: User gets an answer and can see where it came from

steps.system_response: Streams the response inside a provenance envelope
steps.failure_path: Provider unavailable -> UNAVAILABLE state; input preserved; retry offered

steps.system_response: Shows AI involvement, provider/model if known, sources if available

screens.name: Confirmation
screens.purpose: Know the outcome and next step

steps.system_response: Validates on blur/submit, keeps input on error

Network failure -> OFFLINE state; submission retried safely

steps.system_response: Shows the result and the next step

principles.name: Visibility of system status
principles.user_problem: Users act blindly when the system hides what it is doing.
principles.application: Every async action exposes LOADING and a terminal SUCCESS/ERROR with a live-region announcement.
principles.tradeoff: More states to design and test.
principles.a11y_effect: Status changes are announced via polite live regions.
principles.responsive_effect: Status stays visible when layouts collapse (never inside a collapsed drawer only).
principles.implementation_effect: Components expose explicit async state props, not implicit spinners.

effects.value: Async actions render LOADING then SUCCESS or ERROR; never a silent completion.

principles.name: Error prevention and recovery
principles.user_problem: Irreversible mistakes and unrecoverable errors.
principles.application: Destructive actions require confirmation naming the object; errors state cause and a recovery action.
principles.tradeoff: Adds a confirmation step to destructive paths.
principles.a11y_effect: Error text is programmatically associated with the field (aria-describedby).
principles.responsive_effect: Confirmation surfaces become full-width sheets on narrow viewports.
principles.implementation_effect: Form controls carry error message slots and recovery handlers.

effects.value: Error messages state what happened, why, and the next recovery action.
Destructive actions: explicit confirmation naming the affected object; undo where the backend supports it.
Errors are identified in text and linked to the field.

principles.name: User control and freedom
principles.user_problem: Users get trapped in flows they cannot leave or undo.
principles.application: Every step offers back/cancel without data loss; drafts persist.
principles.tradeoff: Draft persistence needs storage and conflict handling.
principles.a11y_effect: Focus returns to a logical element after cancel.
principles.responsive_effect: Back/cancel stay reachable in the collapsed layout.
principles.implementation_effect: Flow state is serializable so drafts survive navigation.

effects.value: Multi-step flows keep back/cancel available and preserve entered data.
Draft state persists across navigation; STALE drafts are labeled with their age.

principles.name: Recognition over recall
principles.user_problem: Users must remember identifiers, filters, or prior choices.
principles.application: Show current filters, selections, and recent items in place.
principles.a11y_effect: Active filters are exposed as a labeled list, not color alone.
principles.responsive_effect: Filter chips WRAP, then collapse into a count + drawer on narrow viewports.
principles.implementation_effect: Filter state lives in the URL for shareability and back-button support.

effects.value: Active filters/selections are always visible with a single clear-all control.
WRAP

principles.name: Proximity and common region
principles.user_problem: Related controls read as unrelated noise.
principles.application: Group related fields/metrics in labeled regions; spacing inside groups is tighter than between groups.
principles.a11y_effect: Groups use fieldset/legend or region landmarks with names.
principles.responsive_effect: Groups STACK as units; they never split across columns.
principles.implementation_effect: Spacing uses semantic tokens (inline < stack < panel).

effects.value: Spacing hierarchy: semantic.space.inline < semantic.space.stack < semantic.space.panel.
Visual groups are programmatic groups (fieldset/legend, labeled regions).

principles.name: Progressive disclosure
principles.user_problem: Everything-at-once screens overload working memory.
principles.application: Primary fields and metrics first; advanced options behind an explicit disclosure.
principles.a11y_effect: Disclosures use aria-expanded and keep focus in place.
principles.responsive_effect: Secondary panels COLLAPSE before primary content shrinks.
principles.implementation_effect: Disclosure components expose EXPANDED state.

effects.value: COLLAPSE

principles.name: Hick's law — limit simultaneous choices
principles.user_problem: Too many equal-weight choices stall the decision.
principles.application: One primary call to action per view; secondary actions are visually subordinate.
principles.a11y_effect: The primary action is first in reading and focus order.
principles.responsive_effect: Secondary actions move into a menu before the primary shrinks.
principles.implementation_effect: CTA components accept a single `primary` variant per region.

effects.value: Exactly one primary action per view; secondary actions use the subordinate variant.
single dominant action per view

principles.name: Fitts's law — target size and distance
principles.user_problem: Small or distant targets cause missed taps and slow pointing.
principles.application: Interactive targets are at least 24x24 CSS px (WCAG 2.2 SC 2.5.8), 44x44 for primary touch actions.
principles.a11y_effect: Meets WCAG 2.2 SC 2.5.8 Target Size (Minimum).
principles.responsive_effect: Primary actions go FULL_WIDTH on narrow touch viewports.
principles.implementation_effect: Buttons enforce a min-block-size token.

effects.value: Interactive targets are at least 24x24 CSS px; primary touch targets 44x44.
FULL_WIDTH

principles.name: Jakob's law — follow platform conventions
principles.user_problem: Novel interaction patterns force users to relearn basics.
principles.application: Use native controls and standard placements; nonstandard interactions must justify themselves.
principles.tradeoff: Less room for novelty in core controls.
principles.a11y_effect: Native elements carry correct roles and keyboard behavior by default.
principles.responsive_effect: Standard navigation transforms (MENU/DRAWER) instead of bespoke gestures.
principles.implementation_effect: Prefer semantic HTML elements over div-based widgets.

effects.value: Core controls are native elements (button, a, input, select, dialog) before any custom widget.

principles.name: Tesler's law — own the irreducible complexity
principles.user_problem: Pushing complexity onto users produces errors and abandonment.
principles.application: The system pre-fills, validates, and explains; users confirm rather than compute.
principles.tradeoff: Moves logic into the backend contract.
principles.a11y_effect: Explanations are text, not tooltips-only.
principles.responsive_effect: Explanations remain inline on narrow viewports.
principles.implementation_effect: Backend contracts return derived values with provenance.

effects.value: Derived values show how they were derived (source + formula) where users act on them.

principles.name: Von Restorff — reserve distinctiveness
principles.user_problem: When everything is emphasized nothing is.
principles.application: Only the P0 element and critical status get the accent treatment.
principles.a11y_effect: Distinctiveness never relies on color alone.
principles.responsive_effect: Accent emphasis survives stacking (it moves with the P0 region).
principles.implementation_effect: Accent tokens are only mapped to primary/critical variants.

effects.value: accent reserved for the P0 action and critical status only

principles.name: Truthful progress
principles.user_problem: Fake progress bars and invented ETAs destroy trust.
principles.application: Show determinate progress only when the backend reports it; otherwise indeterminate + elapsed time.
principles.tradeoff: Less reassuring than a fabricated percentage.
principles.a11y_effect: Progress uses role=progressbar with aria-valuenow only when determinate.
principles.responsive_effect: Progress stays in the primary region when layouts stack.
principles.implementation_effect: Progress components accept `determinate: false` without a value.

effects.value: Determinate progress only from backend-reported values; never a synthetic percentage or ETA.

principles.name: Visual hierarchy through salience budget
principles.user_problem: Users cannot find the primary task among decoration.
principles.application: Salience is budgeted: P0 strongest, P3 never outweighs P0.
principles.a11y_effect: Heading levels mirror the visual hierarchy.
principles.responsive_effect: PRIORITY_REDUCTION drops P3 before compressing P0.
principles.implementation_effect: Regions carry priority + emphasis metadata.

effects.value: Salience budget: P0 > P1 > P2 > P3; P3 regions are removed first under constraint.
Heading structure mirrors the visual hierarchy.

principles.name: Immediate, proportionate feedback
principles.user_problem: Actions without feedback get repeated or abandoned.
principles.application: Every press shows PRESSED within one frame and a result within the async contract.
principles.a11y_effect: Feedback is perceivable without motion or color.
principles.responsive_effect: Feedback anchors to the control, not a region that may collapse.
principles.implementation_effect: Controls expose PRESSED and disabled-while-pending states.

effects.value: Feedback motion <= semantic.motion.duration.feedback; disabled under prefers-reduced-motion.

principles.name: Forms: labels, inline validation, preserved input
principles.user_problem: Unlabeled fields and late validation cause rework.
principles.application: Persistent visible labels; validate on blur/submit, never on first keystroke; keep input on error.
principles.a11y_effect: Labels are programmatic; required state is text, not asterisk color.
principles.responsive_effect: Fields STACK single-column on narrow viewports.
principles.implementation_effect: Field components expose VALID/INVALID/WARNING/READ_ONLY.

effects.value: Every input has a persistent visible label.
STACK

principles.name: Search, filter, sort
principles.user_problem: Users cannot narrow large collections.
principles.application: Search is debounced, results count is announced, empty results suggest recovery.
principles.a11y_effect: Result counts announced via live region.
principles.responsive_effect: Filters move into a DRAWER on narrow viewports.
principles.implementation_effect: Query state is URL-backed.

effects.value: DRAWER

principles.name: Designed empty, loading, and error states
principles.user_problem: Blank screens look broken; spinners hide structure.
principles.application: Skeletons mirror final layout; empty states explain and offer the first action; errors offer retry.
principles.tradeoff: Three extra designs per data surface.
principles.a11y_effect: Skeletons are aria-hidden with a live 'Loading' status.
principles.responsive_effect: Empty states keep the primary action visible at every width.
principles.implementation_effect: Data components expose SKELETON/EMPTY/ERROR/STALE.

principles.name: Modal discipline
principles.user_problem: Modals interrupt and trap focus incorrectly.
principles.application: Modals only for decisions that block progress; focus is trapped and restored.
principles.a11y_effect: dialog element with focus trap and Escape to close.
principles.responsive_effect: Modals become full-screen sheets on narrow viewports.
principles.implementation_effect: Use the native <dialog> element.

effects.value: Dialogs trap focus while open and restore it to the invoking control on close.

principles.name: Semantic zoom
principles.user_problem: Shrinking a desktop layout produces an unusable mobile one.
principles.application: Responsive changes transform representation (table -> list, sidebar -> drawer), not just scale.
principles.a11y_effect: Reflow at 320 CSS px without two-dimensional scrolling (SC 1.4.10).
principles.responsive_effect: Each region declares its transform.
principles.implementation_effect: Container queries where regions are reused.

effects.value: Content reflows at 320 CSS px without two-dimensional scrolling (data tables excepted with scroll containers).
SCROLL

principles.name: Full keyboard operability
principles.user_problem: Keyboard and switch users are locked out.
principles.application: Every interaction has a keyboard path; focus is always visible and never obscured.
principles.tradeoff: Custom widgets need roving tabindex work.
principles.a11y_effect: WCAG 2.2 SC 2.1.1 Keyboard, 2.4.7 Focus Visible, 2.4.11 Focus Not Obscured.
principles.responsive_effect: Sticky headers must not cover the focused element.
principles.implementation_effect: Focus ring uses semantic.color.focus-ring.

effects.value: KEYBOARD
Sticky/fixed regions never fully hide the focused element.

principles.name: Bidirectional layout
principles.user_problem: Mirrored locales break physical-direction layouts.
principles.application: Use logical properties (inline-start/end) everywhere; icons with direction mirror.
principles.a11y_effect: Reading order matches visual order in both directions.
principles.responsive_effect: Transforms are expressed in logical axes.
principles.implementation_effect: No left/right CSS in components.

effects.value: Layout uses logical properties only (margin-inline-start, inset-inline-end).
direction-agnostic logical geometry

principles.name: Truthful AI provenance
principles.user_problem: Users over-trust or mis-attribute machine output.
principles.application: AI output is wrapped in one trust envelope stating involvement, known provider/model, sources, and review status; no decorative confidence.
principles.a11y_effect: Provenance is text, reachable by keyboard, announced when streaming completes.
principles.responsive_effect: The provenance label never collapses away on narrow viewports.
principles.implementation_effect: A single AITrustEnvelope scope per AI response.

effects.value: AI content is labeled AI-generated or AI-assisted; confidence is shown only from a calibrated backend value, otherwise 'Confidence not measured'.

principles.name: Human approval is a first-class state
principles.user_problem: Users cannot tell draft, pending, and approved work apart.
principles.application: PENDING_APPROVAL, APPROVED, REJECTED are distinct in text and icon, not color alone.
principles.a11y_effect: Status is exposed as text.
principles.responsive_effect: Status badges stay attached to their item when lists stack.
principles.implementation_effect: Status comes from the backend lifecycle, never inferred in the client.

principles.name: Degraded-network resilience
principles.user_problem: Live surfaces silently show stale data when the connection drops.
principles.application: OFFLINE and STALE are explicit; reconnection is automatic with a visible manual retry.
principles.a11y_effect: Connection changes announced politely.
principles.responsive_effect: Connection status remains visible in collapsed layouts.
principles.implementation_effect: Stream/socket clients expose connection state and clean up on unmount.

effects.value: Streams, sockets, observers, and timers are cleaned up on unmount.

principles.name: Motion is optional
principles.user_problem: Motion causes vestibular harm and distracts.
principles.application: All non-essential motion is disabled under prefers-reduced-motion; meaning never depends on motion.
principles.tradeoff: Some delight is lost for those users.
principles.a11y_effect: WCAG 2.2 SC 2.3.3 Animation from Interactions (AAA) respected via reduced-motion.
principles.responsive_effect: No motion-dependent reveal of content at any width.
principles.implementation_effect: Motion reads semantic.motion tokens and a reduced-motion guard.

effects.value: prefers-reduced-motion: reduce disables non-essential animation; state changes remain perceivable statically.

principles.name: Structured density for expert users
principles.user_problem: Experts are slowed by consumer-grade whitespace.
principles.application: Denser rows with strict alignment and tabular numerals; density never drops below target sizes.
principles.a11y_effect: Density respects the 24px minimum target size.
principles.responsive_effect: Density relaxes on touch viewports.
principles.implementation_effect: Density is a token scale, not ad hoc spacing.

effects.value: HIGH
Numeric data uses tabular numerals and right alignment.

principles.name: Product-specific signature
principles.user_problem: Template-looking pages are indistinguishable and untrustworthy.
principles.application: One product-specific signature element derived from the brand thesis replaces generic decoration.
principles.a11y_effect: Signature is decorative-only (aria-hidden) or has a text equivalent.
principles.responsive_effect: Signature scales down or drops (P3) before content.
principles.implementation_effect: Signature is a single component, not scattered effects.

effects.value: Replace generic decoration (gradients, glows, floating blobs) with one brand-derived signature element.
